meta.title: Synthetic Harness City
meta.source: Illustrative synthetic profiles only; not audited repository results

ORI-01.t: README exists and has a setup or usage section
ORI-01.w: Baseline human orientation; agents read it first.

ORI-02.w: Shows the maintainers thought about agents at all.

ORI-03.w: Documents the human workflow that agents should mirror.

ORI-04.t: Agent file names build, test and lint commands
ORI-04.w: The first thing an agent needs is how to verify its work.

ORI-05.w: A directory map saves most exploratory searching.

ORI-06.t: Agent file states conventions or boundaries (do, do not)

ORI-07.t: Architecture or design overview document exists
ORI-07.w: Explains why the code looks the way it does.

ORI-08.t: AGENTS.md is canonical; tool-specific files point to it instead of duplicating
ORI-08.w: One source of truth keeps Claude and Copilot behavior identical.

ORI-09.t: No drift between agent files, README and runner targets
ORI-09.w: Contradicting instructions are worse than none.

ORI-10.t: Nested or scoped instructions for large components
ORI-10.w: Monorepos need per-component guidance, not one giant file.

VER-01.w: No tests means no feedback loop.

VER-02.w: No tests means no feedback loop.

VER-03.w: Configured frameworks run the same way for everyone.

VER-04.w: Configured frameworks run the same way for everyone.

VER-05.w: Tests that only run locally rot.

VER-06.w: Tests that only run locally rot.

VER-07.t: Tests gate merges (CI runs on pull requests)
VER-07.w: Enforcement means a failing test blocks the change.

VER-08.t: Test dependencies are declared and pinned or locked
VER-08.w: Agents get the same environment as CI.

VER-09.t: Fast subset exists (markers, scopes, or separate unit and e2e targets)
VER-09.w: Agents iterate on seconds-long checks, not hour-long suites. Speed is inferred from config only.

VER-10.w: Shows which code the tests actually touch.

VER-11.t: Test layout is documented for agents (where tests live, how to run one)
VER-11.w: Running one test is the agent's main inner loop.

STA-01.w: Mechanical style checks remove a whole class of review noise.

STA-02.w: Mechanical style checks remove a whole class of review noise.

STA-03.t: Python lint runs in CI or a hook
STA-03.w: Config without enforcement is a suggestion.

STA-04.t: Node lint runs in CI or a hook
STA-04.w: Config without enforcement is a suggestion.

STA-05.t: Formatter is enforced (check mode in CI, or a formatter hook that CI runs)
STA-05.w: Formatting disputes should never reach a reviewer.

STA-06.t: Python type checking configured and enforced
STA-06.w: Types give agents precise, machine-readable contracts.

STA-07.t: TypeScript type check enforced (tsc --noEmit or equivalent)
STA-07.w: Types give agents precise, machine-readable contracts.

STA-08.t: One configuration per tool (no conflicting duplicate configs)
STA-08.w: Duplicate configs make results depend on the working directory.

STA-09.t: Linter output is actionable (rule ids, file and line)
STA-09.w: Agents fix what they can locate; a wall of text is skipped.

TRG-02.t: Git hooks run lint or format
TRG-02.w: Cheap checks belong at commit time.

TRG-03.t: Git hooks run tests or a fast check target

TRG-04.t: Hooks are versioned in the repo and installed by a documented step
TRG-04.w: A hook nobody installs does nothing.

TRG-05.t: Agent hooks configured (e.g. .claude/settings.json hooks, Copilot equivalents)
TRG-05.w: Lets the repo fire checks right after an agent edits files.

TRG-06.t: Agent hooks and Git hooks call the same entry points (no duplicated logic)
TRG-06.w: Identical behavior no matter who or what triggers the check.

ENT-01.t: A task runner defines at least one target (Taskfile, Makefile, justfile, package.json scripts, tox, nox, poe)
ENT-01.w: Commands that live in a file can be found and reused.

ENT-02.t: Standard targets defined (test, lint, and one of check/ci/verify)

ENT-03.t: Targets are documented (description fields, help target, or README section)
ENT-03.w: Self-describing runners guide humans and agents alike.

ENT-04.t: Setup is one command (install or bootstrap target)
ENT-04.w: A new clone should reach a working state without a wiki trip.

ENT-05.t: One entry point is documented as the way for agents
ENT-05.w: One interface to learn instead of five tool invocations.

ENT-06.t: A preflight or doctor target checks the environment
ENT-06.w: Agents fail early and clearly when tools are missing.

ENT-07.t: Runner supports scoped runs (per package, per path or per test)
ENT-07.w: Narrow runs keep the agent loop fast.

CIP-01.w: Without CI nothing is enforced for contributors.

CIP-02.t: CI runs both lint and tests

CIP-03.t: CI runs on pull requests and on the default branch
CIP-03.w: Checks must run before and after merge.

CIP-04.t: CI uses dependency caching or lockfile installs
CIP-04.w: Reproducible and fast; also shows lockfile discipline.

CIP-05.t: CI calls the local entry point (task, make, npm run, nox) instead of duplicating commands
CIP-05.w: What passes locally passes in CI, and the reverse.

CIP-06.t: Matrix covers supported versions (Python or Node versions, OS)
CIP-06.w: Documents the supported range as executable fact.

CIP-07.t: Dependency and workflow updates automated (Dependabot or Renovate)
CIP-07.w: Keeps the harness itself from decaying.

DOC-01.t: A docs directory or documentation site exists

DOC-02.t: Docs build or link check runs in CI
DOC-02.w: Broken docs are found by machines, not by readers.

DOC-03.w: Consistent structure helps parsing by tools and agents.

DOC-04.t: Front matter or schema enforced on docs
DOC-04.w: Metadata that is enforced is metadata that can be trusted.

DOC-05.t: Decisions recorded (ADR directory with recent entries)
DOC-05.w: Gives agents the reasons, not just the code.

DOC-06.t: Documentation references resolve (no dead paths or commands in docs)
DOC-06.w: Stale references are the most common way docs mislead agents.

lim: Illustrative synthetic levels only; no repository was audited and no checks or runtime behavior were observed.
